#lang ivy1.7

# Source: https://github.com/sat-group/cfg-enum/blob/master/examples/decentralized-lock.ivy

type node
type time

relation le(X: time, Y: time)
axiom forall X : time . le(X, X)
axiom forall X : time . forall Y : time . le(X, Y) & le(Y, Z) -> le(X, Z)
axiom forall X : time . forall Y : time . (le(X, Y) & le(Y, X)) -> X = Y
axiom forall X : time . forall Y : time . le(X, Y) | le(Y, X)

relation has_lock(X: node)
relation msg(X: node, Y: node, E: time)
relation gt(T: time, X: node)

individual first: node
individual zero: time
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max: time
axiom le(X, max)

after init {
	has_lock(X) := (X = first);
	msg(X,Y,T) := false;
	gt(T, X) := (T ~= zero);
}

action take_lock(x: node, y: node, t: time) = {
    require msg(x, y, t);
    require gt(t, y);
    has_lock(y) := true;
    gt(T, y) := true if ~le(T, t) else false;
}

action release_lock(x: node, y : node, t: time) = {
    require has_lock(x);
    require gt(t, x);
    has_lock(x) := false;
    msg(x, y, t) := true;
}

export take_lock
export release_lock

# safety property

invariant [safety_1] ~(X ~= Y & has_lock(X) & has_lock(Y))

invariant [inv1] has_lock(X) & has_lock(Y) -> X = Y
invariant [inv2] msg(X, Y, T) -> has_lock(X)
invariant [inv3] gt(T, X) & has_lock(X) -> ~le(T, T) # This is a placeholder, let's refine.
# Actually, let's look at the logic again.
# The lock is held by at most one node.
# When a node releases the lock, it sends a message.
# The message contains a timestamp.

# The key is that the lock is either held by a node or is in a message.

invariant [inv1] has_lock(X) & has_lock(Y) -> X = Y

invariant [inv3] msg(X, Y, T) & msg(X, Z, T2) -> Y = Z
invariant [inv4] has_lock(X) & msg(X, Y, T) -> false
invariant [inv5] msg(X, Y, T) & msg(Z, W, T2) -> (X = Z & Y = W & T = T2) # Only one message at a time? Or maybe just that messages are unique?
# The counterexample shows multiple messages can exist.

# So `gt(T, y)` means `T` is greater than the last timestamp seen by `y`.
# Let's try:
invariant [inv_gt] gt(T, X) <-> ~exists T_old. (le(T_old, T) & ~le(T, T_old) & ~le(T_old, T_old)) # This is getting complicated.
# Let's simplify. The `gt` relation is just a way to order messages.

invariant [inv_msg_lock2] msg(X, Y, T) -> ~has_lock(Y) # This might be too strong.

invariant [inv_msg_lock] msg(X, Y, T) -> ~has_lock(X)
invariant [inv_msg_lock2] has_lock(X) & has_lock(Y) -> X = Y

invariant [inv_msg_lock3] msg(X, Y, T) & has_lock(Z) -> X ~= Z

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~held(N)
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant held(N) -> le(ep(M), ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(E, ep(M))
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(M))

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#
# New property defined: If a node holds the lock, then its epoch is the highest.
# Modification: Got rid of first non-zero epoch (since not necessary).

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] held(N1) -> le(ep(N2), ep(N1))

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N) -> ~held(N)
invariant locked(E, N) -> ~held(N)
invariant transfer(E1, N1) & transfer(E2, N2) -> E1 = E2 & N1 = N2
invariant locked(E1, N1) & locked(E2, N2) -> E1 = E2 & N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(ep(M), E)
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(ep(M), E)

**Exploring Ring Protocol Logic**

I'm currently grappling with the nuances of modeling a leader election protocol on a ring. Specifically, I'm focused on formalizing the total order for nodes, represented by `le(N0, N1)`, and the ring's structural definition through the `btw(W, X, Y)` relation. My aim is to accurately capture the `leader(N)` predicate.

**Refining Leader Election Logic**

I'm refining the `recv` action. If a node `n` receives its own message (`sender = n`), it's declared the leader. This is key to the election termination. I'm also analyzing a counterexample where `leader(0)` incorrectly becomes true, indicating a potential flaw when `le(1, 0)` is false.

**Validating Message Forwarding**

I'm re-evaluating the message forwarding logic. It appears a message `sender` only persists if `le(n, sender)` holds true at node `n`. This is crucial for ensuring only the true leader's message circulates back to it.

**Proving Message Persistence**

I'm focusing on the invariant `pending(S, N) -> le(N, S)`. My current analysis suggests this holds true. If a message `S` is pending at node `N`, it implies that `le(N, S)` must be true, indicating `S` is greater than or equal to `N` in the established order.

**Investigating Ring Connectivity**

I'm exploring the implication of `send(n, next)` setting `pending(n, next)`. My current hypothesis is that this action should necessitate `le(next, n)` being true for the message to be considered validly sent within the ring's ordering. This seems crucial for the `recv` logic.

**Verifying Message Propagation**

#lang ivy1.7

#
# An Ivy model of the toy lock example from https://github.com/Microsoft/Ironclad/blob/master/ironfleet/src/Dafny/Distributed/Protocol/Lock/Node.i.dfy
#
# For a description of the protocol, see the IronFleet paper
# (https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2015/10/ironfleet.pdf),
# Figure 4
#

# A total order helper module
module total_order(r) = {
    axiom r(X,X)                        # Reflexivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, Z) -> r(X, Z)  # Transitivity
    axiom r(X, Y) & r(Y, X) -> X = Y    # Anti-symmetry
    axiom r(X, Y) | r(Y, X)             # Totality
}

################################################################################
#
# Types, relations and functions describing state of the network
#
################################################################################

type node
type epoch

# epochs are totally ordered with a least element called zero
relation le(X:epoch, Y:epoch)
instantiate total_order(le)
individual zero:epoch
axiom le(zero, X)
individual max:epoch
axiom le(X, max)

function ep(N:node) : epoch # ep(n) is the current epoch of node n

relation held(N:node) # held(n) is true iff the lock is currently held by node n

# transfer messages
relation transfer(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message destination

# locked messages
relation locked(E:epoch, N:node)  # the node is the message source

################################################################################
#
# Protocol description
#
################################################################################
individual first:node
individual firste:epoch
axiom firste ~= zero

after init {
    # initially exactly one node holds the lock, and everyone has epoch zero
    held(X) := X=first;
    ep(N) := firste if N = first else zero;
    transfer(E, N) := false;
    locked(E, N) := false;
}

action grant(n1:node, n2:node, e:epoch) = {
    # release the lock and send a transfer message
    require held(n1);
    require ~le(e, ep(n1));   # jump to some strictly higher epoch
    transfer(e, n2) := true;
    held(n1) := false;
}

action accept(n:node, e:epoch) = {
    # receive a transfer message and take the lock, sending a locked message
    require transfer(e,n);
#    transfer(e,n) := *;
    if ~le(e, ep(n)) {
        held(n) := true;
        ep(n) := e;
        locked(e, n) := true;
    };
}

export grant
export accept

# the safety property
invariant [safety_1] locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2

invariant held(N1) & held(N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant transfer(E, N1) & transfer(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant le(firste, ep(N)) | ~held(N)
invariant locked(E, N1) & locked(E, N2) -> N1 = N2
invariant locked(E, N) -> le(E, ep(N))
invariant transfer(E, N) -> le(firste, E)
